speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough for about three months now, and it produces small amounts of white phlegm. I haven't coughed up any blood, but I do get quite short of breath when I try to climb stairs. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of three months suggests a chronic condition rather than an acute infection. To better understand the severity of your shortness of breath, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles recently? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation of lungs. Flattened diaphragm. No focal lung opacities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of hyperinflation and a flattened diaphragm are classic signs of air trapping. Have you noticed a history of smoking or exposure to significant dust or chemical fumes?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I smoked a pack a day for forty years, though I quit five years ago. I also worked as a construction worker for many years, so I've likely been exposed to a lot of dust and fumes. I want to emphasize that, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
